questions.question: When is a system of equations called a linear system?
options: At least one equation is quadratic.
Every equation in the system is linear.
The variables are written in alphabetical order.
The system has exactly two equations.
questions.explanation: A system is called linear exactly when every equation in it is linear (first-power variables, scalar coefficients).

option_explanations: A quadratic equation makes the system nonlinear, not linear.

Linearity requires each equation to have variables only to the first power with scalar coefficients, e.g. $a_{i1}x_1+\cdots+a_{in}x_n=b_i$; the names or alphabetical ordering of the unknowns are pure notation and do not affect whether the powers are linear.
The number of equations does not decide linearity.
